## touch-browser v0.7.0

This release makes the local first-use path clearer and safer. The main changes are a new `quickstart` command, beginner-oriented summaries on the JSON output, and more forgiving handling for empty session files created by common shell workflows.

### Added

- Added `touch-browser quickstart` with the recommended local flow, success signals, safe defaults, and common pitfalls.
- Added `beginnerQuickStart` to `capabilities` / `status` so agents and humans see the same first-use path.
- Added top-level `summary` fields for `open`, `quick`, and `extract`, including page title/source type for opens and claim counts/reusable counts for evidence checks.
- Added top-level `claimOutcomes` to evidence command output so callers do not need to know the nested report path for the common case.

### Changed

- Changed the recommended first call to `touch-browser quickstart`.
- Updated README and CLI surface docs to match the new beginner-facing output contract.
- Bumped Rust workspace, CLI runtime, MCP package, MCP server descriptors, workflow metadata, Glama Docker install pin, and standalone lifecycle expectations to `0.7.0`.

### Fixed

- Fixed empty `--session-file` handling for new browser-backed opens and extracts; an empty file is now treated as a new session target and overwritten with a valid session.
- Improved empty session read errors with an actionable recovery command instead of a raw JSON EOF parse failure.

### Verification

- Local Rust CLI lib tests passed.
- Local lint, format, typecheck, clippy, contracts, Rust workspace tests, Playwright adapter gate, and eval gate passed.
- Local CLI smoke passed for `quickstart`, compact `status`, `quick` summaries, browser-backed open summaries, empty session-file recovery, and help output.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/nangman-infra/touch-browser/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0
